title: Amniocentesis
what: Guided by ultrasound, the doctor uses a thin needle through your belly to take a little amniotic fluid. It is tested for your baby's chromosomes and genes.
why: When screening shows a high risk, the ultrasound finds something unusual, or there is an inherited condition in the family. Usually after 15 to 16 weeks.
duration: the procedure itself usually takes 15 to 30 minutes; first results usually come in a few days, full results in up to 2 to 3 weeks
tell_doctor: Your blood type and Rh factor
Infections such as hepatitis or HIV. This matters for your baby's safety
Any bleeding or pain in recent days

prepare.title: Your decision
prepare.text: A genetics doctor will explain beforehand why it is done, the risks, and what the test shows. You sign a consent form.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: You usually need a blood test, blood type and Rh, and sometimes infection tests.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You can usually have a light meal. For your bladder, follow the clinic's advice.

prepare.title: Rest
prepare.text: Keep the day after free. You need to take it easy.

steps: You lie on your back, and the doctor does an ultrasound to find a good spot
The skin on your belly is cleaned with antiseptic
Guided by ultrasound, a thin needle is passed through your belly
A little fluid is drawn, usually in under a minute
The needle is removed, and your baby's heartbeat is checked
feel: A prick and a feeling of pressure or cramping in your belly
Feeling nervous is normal. You can ask someone to hold your hand
Afterward, a pulling feeling low in your belly for a few hours
after: You usually rest at the clinic for 20 to 30 minutes
On the day and for 1 to 2 days after, take it easy: no lifting or exercise
If you are Rh negative, you usually get an anti-D injection
A genetics doctor will explain the results
red_flags: Fluid leaking from the vagina: see a doctor urgently or call emergency services
Bleeding or severe belly pain: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F) or chills: see a doctor urgently
Your baby is moving much less than usual: see a doctor urgently

faq.q: Is amniocentesis dangerous for my baby?
faq.a: There is a small risk of miscarriage. Your doctor will explain it for your situation before the procedure.
It is usually bearable: like a shot and pressure in your belly. It does not last long.

faq.q: Do I have to have it?
faq.a: No. It is your choice. Your doctor will help you weigh the benefits and risks.

reminders.text: Amniocentesis tomorrow. Bring your screening and ultrasound results. Ask someone to take you home.
